newsitem.title: DENMARK: ISS sees better times after U.S. sale.
newsitem.headline: ISS sees better times after U.S. sale.

text.p: Danish cleaning group ISS -- battered by false accounting in its former U.S. unit -- reported on Tuesday a 1.86 billion crown net loss for 1996, compared to a revised 20 million crown profit the year before.
But the group said that with last December's sale of ISS Inc ending its liablities it looked foward to improved profitablity and a more stable share price in 1997.

"Following the divestment of ISS Inc, ISS has reduced turnover, but profitablity and key figures in all areas have improved substantially and the uncertainty arising from ISS Inc that has caused substantial fluctuations in ISS' share price during the past year has been eliminated," its 1996 report said.
The market apparently agreed and despite the bottom-line loss the group's share had traded up to 181 crowns by 1040 GMT, from Monday's closing 178.2.
"After the sale of ISS Inc the ISS group has a higher organic growth rate, a better profit margin, improved free cash flow, lower debtor days and an improved equity ratio," the report said.
"Organic growth will be supplemented by strategic acquisitions, for which there are many potential candidates," it added.
Group turnover was up by a billion crowns, to 15.396 from 1995's 14,391, and operating profit rose to 619 million crowns in 1996 from 572 million the year before.
Analysts' average forecasts were for turnover of 15.750 billion crowns, with operating profit of 630 million.
